title: Molecular locking of lithium ions for improved efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells - Nature Energy
byline: Pan; Tengfei; Ren; Biyun; Yang; Yao; Qing; Wang; Kaiyu; Qian; Shijing; Zhao; Xin; Yajing; Xia; Yingdong; Chao; Lingfeng; Chen; Yonghua; Huang; Wei
html:
Abstract

The hole-transport material 2,2′,7,7′-tetrakis(N,N-di-p-methoxyphenyl-amine)-9,9′-spirobifluorene (Spiro-OMeTAD) is commonly used in perovskite solar cells but suffers from instabilities due to the hygroscopicity and lithium ion migration induced by additives, such as lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and 4-tert-butylpyridine (tBP), in its formulation. Here we show a molecular locking strategy by designing phosphonate-based molecules with extended cyano chains, enabling dual-site coordination with lithium ions to regulate ion mobility and stabilize the lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide/tBP dopant environment. Meanwhile, the phosphonate-based molecule reduces tBP loss, enhances the thermomechanical robustness of the Spiro-OMeTAD matrix, mitigates dopant redistribution and stabilizes the interface. These coupled effects collectively improve device stability under illumination, thermal and electrical stresses. The optimized n–i–p perovskite solar cells achieve a champion efficiency of 26.73% and retain 95% of the initial efficiency after 1,000 h under maximum power point tracking (International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS)-L-1), 95% after 1,000 h at 85 °C (ISOS-L-2) and 91% after 1,600 h under 1.5 V bias (ISOS-V-1).
